# JsonContainerTrait in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/trait.JsonContainerTrait.html

```
pub trait JsonContainerTrait {
    type
```
[ObjectType](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.ObjectType);
    type [ArrayType](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.ArrayType);
    // Required methods
    fn [as_object](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_object)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&Self::[ObjectType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonContainerTrait.html#associatedtype.ObjectType)>;
[as_array](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_array)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&Self::[ArrayType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonContainerTrait.html#associatedtype.ArrayType)>;
}## Expand description

A trait for all JSON object or array values. Used by `Value`.

The `Option<V: JsonContainerTrait>` and `Result<V: JsonContainerTrait, E>` also implement this
trait. The `Option::None` or `Result::Err(_)` will be viewed as a null value.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#406)#### fn [as_object](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_object)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&Self::[ObjectType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonContainerTrait.html#associatedtype.ObjectType)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#406)

#### fn [as_object](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_object)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&Self::[ObjectType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonContainerTrait.html#associatedtype.ObjectType)>

Returns the object if `self` is an `object`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, object, JsonContainerTrait, JsonValueTrait, Value};
let value: Value = sonic_rs::from_str(r#"{"a": 1, "b": true}"#).unwrap();
assert!(value.is_object());
assert_eq!(value.as_object(), Some(&object! {"a": 1, "b": true}));
```
Returns the array if `self` is an `array`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{array, json, JsonContainerTrait, JsonValueTrait, Value};
let value: Value = sonic_rs::from_str(r#"[1, 2, 3]"#).unwrap();
assert!(value.is_array());
assert_eq!(value.as_array(), Some(&array![1, 2, 3]));
```

# JsonValueMutTrait in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/trait.JsonValueMutTrait.html

pub trait JsonValueMutTrait {
    type

}## Expand description

A trait for all mutable JSON values. Used by mutable `Value`.

The `Option<V: JsonValueMutTrait>` and `Result<V: JsonValueMutTrait, E>` also implement this
trait. The `Option::None` or `Result::Err(_)` will be viewed as a null value.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#445)#### fn [as_object_mut](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_object_mut)(&mut self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&mut Self::[ObjectType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueMutTrait.html#associatedtype.ObjectType)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#445)

#### fn [as_object_mut](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_object_mut)(&mut self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&mut Self::[ObjectType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueMutTrait.html#associatedtype.ObjectType)>

Returns the mutable object if `self` is an `object`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{JsonValueMutTrait, json};
use sonic_rs::Value;
let mut value: Value = sonic_rs::from_str(r#"{"a": 1, "b": true}"#).unwrap();
let obj = value.as_object_mut().unwrap();
obj["a"] = json!(2);
assert_eq!(value, json!({"a": 2, "b": true}));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#459)#### fn [as_array_mut](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_array_mut)(&mut self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&mut Self::[ArrayType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueMutTrait.html#associatedtype.ArrayType)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#459)

#### fn [as_array_mut](https://docs.rs#tymethod.as_array_mut)(&mut self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&mut Self::[ArrayType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueMutTrait.html#associatedtype.ArrayType)>

Returns the mutable array if `self` is an `array`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, JsonValueMutTrait, Value};
let mut value: Value = sonic_rs::from_str(r#"[1, 2, 3]"#).unwrap();
let arr = value.as_array_mut().unwrap();
arr[0] = json!(2);
assert_eq!(value, json!([2, 2, 3]));
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#481-483)#### fn [pointer_mut](https://docs.rs#tymethod.pointer_mut)<P: [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)>(
    &mut self,
    path: P,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&mut Self::[ValueType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueMutTrait.html#associatedtype.ValueType)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#481-483)

#### fn [pointer_mut](https://docs.rs#tymethod.pointer_mut)<P: [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)>(
    &mut self,
    path: P,
) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<&mut Self::[ValueType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueMutTrait.html#associatedtype.ValueType)>

Looks up a value by a path.

The path is an iterator of multiple keys or indexes. It can be a `&[&str]`, `&[usize]`
or a `JsonPointer`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
let data = json!({
    "x": {
        "y": ["z", "zz"]
    }
});
assert_eq!(data.pointer(&["x", "y"] ).unwrap(), &json!(["z", "zz"]));
assert_eq!(data.pointer(&pointer!["x", "y", 1] ).unwrap(), &json!("zz"));
assert_eq!(data.pointer(&["a", "b"]), None);
```
Mutably index into a JSON array or map. A string-like index can be used to access a value in a map, and a usize index can be used to access an element of an array.

Returns `None` if the type of `self` does not match the type of the
index, for example if the index is a string and `self` is an array or a
number. Also returns `None` if the given key does not exist in the map
or the given index is not within the bounds of the array.

```
use sonic_rs::{json, JsonValueMutTrait};
let mut object = json!({ "A": 65, "B": 66, "C": 67 });
*object.get_mut("A").unwrap() = json!(69);
let mut array = json!([ "A", "B", "C" ]);
*array.get_mut(2).unwrap() = json!("D");
```
## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

}## Expand description

A trait for all JSON values. Used by `Value` and `LazyValue`.

The `Option<V: JsonValueTrait>` and `Result<V: JsonValueTrait, E>` also implement this trait.
The `Option::None` or `Result::Err(_)` will be viewed as a null value.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

Gets the type of the value. Returns `JsonType::Null` as default if `self` is `Option::None`
or `Result::Err(_)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{
    value::{JsonType, JsonValueTrait, Value},
    Result,
};
let json: Value = sonic_rs::from_str(r#"{"a": 1, "b": true}"#).unwrap();
assert_eq!(json.get_type(), JsonType::Object);
let v: Option<&Value> = json.get("c");
assert!(v.is_none());
assert_eq!(v.get_type(), JsonType::Null);
let v: Result<Value> = sonic_rs::from_str("invalid json");
assert!(v.is_err());
assert_eq!(v.get_type(), JsonType::Null);
```
Index into a JSON array or map. A string-like index can be used to access a value in a map, and a usize index can be used to access an element of an array.

Returns `None` if the type of `self` does not match the type of the
index, for example if the index is a string and `self` is an array or a
number. Also returns `None` if the given key does not exist in the map
or the given index is not within the bounds of the array.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::value::{JsonType, JsonValueTrait, Value};
let json: Value = sonic_rs::from_str(r#"{"a": 1, "b": true}"#).unwrap();
assert!(json.get("a").is_number());
assert!(json.get("unknown").is_none());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#381-383)#### fn [pointer](https://docs.rs#tymethod.pointer)<P: [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)>(&self, path: P) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self::[ValueType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueTrait.html#associatedtype.ValueType)<'_>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sonic_rs/value/value_trait.rs.html#381-383)

#### fn [pointer](https://docs.rs#tymethod.pointer)<P: [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)>(&self, path: P) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<Self::[ValueType](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueTrait.html#associatedtype.ValueType)<'_>>

Looks up a value by a path.

The path is an iterator of multiple keys or indexes. It can be a `&[&str]`, `&[usize]`
or a `JsonPointer`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, pointer, JsonValueTrait};
let data = json!({
    "x": {
        "y": ["z", "zz"]
    }
});
assert_eq!(data.pointer(&["x", "y"] ).unwrap(), &json!(["z", "zz"]));
assert_eq!(data.pointer(&pointer!["x", "y", 1] ).unwrap(), &json!("zz"));
assert_eq!(data.pointer(&["a", "b"]), None);
```
## Provided Methods[§](https://docs.rs#provided-methods)

Returns true if the `self` value is `null`.

[§](https://docs.rs#notes)Notes

It will Returns true if `self` is `Option::None` or `Result::Err(_)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, JsonValueTrait, Result, Value};
let val = json!(null);
assert!(val.is_null());
let val: Option<&Value> = val.get("unknown");
assert!(val.is_none());
assert!(val.is_null());
let val: Result<Value> = sonic_rs::from_str("invalid json");
assert!(val.is_err());
assert!(val.is_null());
```
Returns true if the value is a number and it is an `f64`.
It will returns false if the value is a `u64` or `i64`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-14)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, JsonValueTrait};
assert!(!json!(123).is_f64()); // false
assert!(!json!(-123).is_f64()); // false
assert!(json!(-1.23).is_f64());
```
Returns true if the value is a integer number and it between `i64::MIN` and `i64::MAX`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, JsonValueTrait};
assert!(json!(-123).is_i64());
assert!(json!(0).is_i64());
assert!(json!(123).is_i64());
assert!(json!(i64::MIN).is_i64());
assert!(json!(i64::MAX).is_i64());
assert!(!json!(u64::MAX).is_i64()); // overflow for i64
assert!(!json!(-1.23).is_i64()); // false
```
Returns true if the value is a integer number and it between `0` and `i64::MAX`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-16)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, JsonValueTrait};
assert!(json!(123).is_u64());
assert!(json!(0).is_u64());
assert!(json!(u64::MAX).is_u64());
assert!(!json!(-123).is_u64());
assert!(!json!(1.23).is_u64());
```
If `self` meets `is_i64`, represent it as i64 if possible. Returns None otherwise.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-17)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, JsonValueTrait};
assert_eq!(json!(123).as_i64(), Some(123));
assert_eq!(json!(-123).as_i64(), Some(-123));
assert_eq!(json!(i64::MAX).as_i64(), Some(i64::MAX));
assert_eq!(json!(u64::MAX).as_i64(), None);
```
If `self` meets `is_i64`, represent it as u64 if possible. Returns None otherwise.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, JsonValueTrait};
assert_eq!(json!(123).as_u64(), Some(123));
assert_eq!(json!(-123).as_u64(), None);
assert_eq!(json!(i64::MAX).as_u64(), Some(i64::MAX as u64));
assert_eq!(json!(u64::MAX).as_u64(), Some(u64::MAX));
```
If `self` is a number, represent it as f64 if possible. Returns None otherwise.
The integer number will be converted to f64.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-19)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::{json, JsonValueTrait};
assert_eq!(json!(123).as_f64(), Some(123 as f64));
assert_eq!(json!(-123).as_f64(), Some(-123 as f64));
assert_eq!(json!(0.123).as_f64(), Some(0.123));
assert_eq!(json!("hello").as_f64(), None);
```

# Serialize in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/trait.Serialize.html

```
pub trait Serialize {
    // Required method
    fn
```
[serialize](https://docs.rs#tymethod.serialize)<S>(
        &self,
        serializer: S,
    ) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<<S as [Serializer](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html)>::[Ok](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html#associatedtype.Ok), <S as [Serializer](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html#associatedtype.Error)>
       where S: [Serializer](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html);
}## Expand description

A **data structure** that can be serialized into any data format supported
by Serde.

Serde provides `Serialize` implementations for many Rust primitive and
standard library types. The complete list is [here](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/index.html). All of
these can be serialized using Serde out of the box.

Additionally, Serde provides a procedural macro called [ serde_derive](https://crates.io/crates/serde_derive) to
automatically generate

`Serialize` implementations for structs and enums in
your program. See the [derive section of the manual](https://serde.rs/derive.html)for how to use this.

In rare cases it may be necessary to implement `Serialize` manually for some
type in your program. See the [Implementing  Serialize](https://serde.rs/impl-serialize.html) section of the
manual for more about this.

Third-party crates may provide `Serialize` implementations for types that
they expose. For example the [ linked-hash-map](https://crates.io/crates/linked-hash-map) crate provides a

[type that is serializable by Serde because the crate provides an implementation of](https://docs.rs/linked-hash-map/*/linked_hash_map/struct.LinkedHashMap.html)

`LinkedHashMap<K, V>``Serialize` for it.## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

[Source](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/serde_core/ser/mod.rs.html#265-267)

#### fn [serialize](https://docs.rs#tymethod.serialize)<S>(
    &self,
    serializer: S,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<<S as [Serializer](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html)>::[Ok](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html#associatedtype.Ok), <S as [Serializer](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html)>::[Error](https://docs.rs/serde_core/1.0.228/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_core/ser/trait.Serializer.html#associatedtype.Error)>

Serialize this value into the given Serde serializer.

See the [Implementing  Serialize](https://serde.rs/impl-serialize.html) section of the manual for more
information about how to implement this method.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use serde::ser::{Serialize, SerializeStruct, Serializer};
struct Person {
    name: String,
    age: u8,
    phones: Vec<String>,
}
// This is what #[derive(Serialize)] would generate.
impl Serialize for Person {
    fn serialize<S>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error>
    where
        S: Serializer,
    {
        let mut s = serializer.serialize_struct("Person", 3)?;
        s.serialize_field("name", &self.name)?;
        s.serialize_field("age", &self.age)?;
        s.serialize_field("phones", &self.phones)?;
        s.end()
    }
}
```
## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety", so this trait is not object safe.*

**crate feature**only.

`rc` and (crate features `std` or `alloc`)Serializing a data structure containing `Rc` will serialize a copy of
the contents of the `Rc` each time the `Rc` is referenced within the
data structure. Serialization will not attempt to deduplicate these
repeated data.

**crate feature**only.

the contents of the `Arc` each time the `Arc` is referenced within the
data structure. Serialization will not attempt to deduplicate these
repeated data.

# from_value in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/fn.from_value.html

## Expand description

Interpret a `sonic_rs::Value` as an instance of type `T`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use serde::Deserialize;
use sonic_rs::json;
#[derive(Deserialize, Debug)]
struct User {
    string: String,
    number: i32,
    array: Vec<String>,
}
 // The type of `j` is `sonic_rs::Value`
 let j = json!({
     "string": "hello",
     "number": 123,
     "array": ["a", "b", "c"],
 });
 let u: User = sonic_rs::from_value(&j).unwrap();
 assert_eq!(u.string, "hello");
 assert_eq!(u.number, 123);
 assert_eq!(u.array, vec!["a", "b", "c"]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

This conversion can fail if the structure of the Value does not match the
structure expected by `T`, for example if `T` is a struct type but the Value
contains something other than a JSON map. It can also fail if the structure
is correct but `T`’s implementation of `Deserialize` decides that something
is wrong with the data, for example required struct fields are missing from
the JSON map or some number is too big to fit in the expected primitive
type.

# get in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/fn.get.html

`pub fn get<'de, Input, Path: `[IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)>(
    json: Input,
    path: Path,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)<[LazyValue](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyValue.html)<'de>>## Expand description

Gets a field from a `path`. And return it as a [ Result<LazyValue>](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyValue.html).

If not found, return an error. If the `path` is empty, return the whole JSON as a `LazyValue`.

The `Item` of the `path` should implement the [ Index](https://docs.rs/trait.Index.html) trait.

The input `json` is allowed to be `&FastStr`, `&[u8]`, `&str`, `&String` or `&bytes::Bytes`.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

The JSON must be valid and well-formed, otherwise it may return unexpected result.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use bytes::Bytes;
use faststr::FastStr;
use sonic_rs::get;
let lv = get(r#"{"a": 1}"#, &["a"]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(lv.as_raw_str(), "1");
/// not found the field "a"
let fs = FastStr::new(r#"{"a": 1}"#);
let lv = get(&fs, &["b"]);
assert!(lv.is_err());
/// the JSON is invalid
let b = Bytes::from(r#"{"a": tru }"#);
let lv = get(&b, &["a"]);
assert!(lv.is_err());
```

# get_by_schema in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/fn.get_by_schema.html

## Expand description

get_by_schema returns new Value from the given schema and json data

This function can be used to query json data on demand.

If a key path, for example [“b”, “b1”] exists in the schema, but does not exist in the data, then the data will be filled with the corresponding default value in the schema.

If a key path does’not exists in the schema, but exists in the data, then the value in the schema will be replaced with the corresponding value in the data.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::json;
let schema = json!({
    "a": null, // default value is `null`
    "b": {
        "b1": {},
        "b2": "default string" // default value is string
    },
    "c": [], // default value is []
});
let data = r#"
{
    "a": {},
    "b": {
        "b1": 123
    },
    "c": [1, 2, 3],
    "d": "balabala..."
}"#;
// parse json data by schem, we can parse into the schema value inplace
let got = sonic_rs::get_by_schema(data, schema).unwrap();
assert_eq!(
    got,
    json!({
        "a": {},
        "b": {
            "b1": 123,
            "b2": "default string"
        },
        "c": [1, 2, 3]
    })
);
```

# get_from_faststr in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/fn.get_from_faststr.html

`pub fn get_from_faststr<Path: `[IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)>(
    json: &[FastStr](https://docs.rs/struct.FastStr.html),
    path: Path,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)<[LazyValue](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyValue.html)<'_>>## Expand description

Gets a field from a `path`. And return it as a [ Result<LazyValue>](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyValue.html).

If not found, return an error. If the `path` is empty, return the whole JSON as a `LazyValue`.

The `Item` of the `path` should implement the [ Index](https://docs.rs/trait.Index.html) trait.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
// get from the &[&str]
let fs = faststr::FastStr::new(r#"{"a": 1}"#);
let lv = get_from_faststr(&fs, &["a"]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(lv.as_raw_str(), "1");
// not found the field "a"
let lv = get_from_faststr(&fs, &["b"]);
assert!(lv.unwrap_err().is_not_found());
// get from the &[usize]
let fs = faststr::FastStr::new(r#"[0, 1, "two"]"#);
let lv = get_from_faststr(&fs, &[2]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(lv.as_raw_str(), "\"two\"");
// get from pointer!
use sonic_rs::pointer;
let fs = faststr::FastStr::new(r#"{"a": [0, 1, "two"]}"#);
let lv = get_from_faststr(&fs, &pointer!["a", 2]).unwrap();
assert_eq!(lv.as_raw_str(), "\"two\"");
/// the type of JSON is unmatched, expect it is a object
let lv = get_from_faststr(&fs, &pointer!["a", "get key from array"]);
assert!(lv.unwrap_err().is_unmatched_type());

`pub unsafe fn get_from_faststr_unchecked<Path: `[IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)>(

# to_array_iter in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/fn.to_array_iter.html

`pub fn to_array_iter<'de, I: `[JsonInput](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonInput.html)<'de>>(json: I) -> [ArrayJsonIter](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayJsonIter.html)<'de> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)## Expand description

Traverse the JSON array text through a lazy iterator. The JSON parsing will doing when iterating.

The item of the iterator is [ Result<LazyValue>](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyValue.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

If the JSON is empty, not array or parse error, it will return Err and `next()` will return
`None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
for (i, ret) in to_array_iter(r#"[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]"#).enumerate() {
    let lv = ret.unwrap(); // get lazyvalue
    assert_eq!(i.to_string(), lv.as_raw_str()); // lv is not parsed
    assert_eq!(i, lv.as_u64().unwrap() as usize);
}
for elem in to_array_iter(r#"[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6"#) {
    // do something for each elem
    // deal with errors when invalid json
    if elem.is_err() {
        assert!(elem
            .unwrap_err()
            .to_string()
            .contains("Expected this character to be either a ',' or a ']'"));
    }
}
```

# to_object_iter in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/fn.to_object_iter.html

`pub fn to_object_iter<'de, I: `[JsonInput](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonInput.html)<'de>>(json: I) -> [ObjectJsonIter](https://docs.rs/struct.ObjectJsonIter.html)<'de> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)## Expand description

Traverse the JSON object text through a lazy iterator. The JSON parsing will doing when iterating.

The item of the iterator is a key-value pair: ([FastStr](https://docs.rs/struct.FastStr.html),
[ Result<LazyValue>](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyValue.html)).

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

If the JSON is empty, not a object or parse error, the result will be Err and the `next()` will
return `None`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use faststr::FastStr;
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
let json = FastStr::from(r#"{"a": null, "b":[1, 2, 3]}"#);
for ret in to_object_iter(&json) {
    assert!(ret.is_ok());
    let (k, v) = ret.unwrap();
    if k == "a" {
        assert!(v.is_null());
    } else if k == "b" {
        assert_eq!(v.as_raw_str(), "[1, 2, 3]");
    }
}
// the JSON is invalid, will report error when encountering the error
for (i, ret) in to_object_iter(r#"{"a": null, "b":[1, 2, 3"#).enumerate() {
    if i == 0 {
        assert!(ret.is_ok());
    }
    if i == 1 {
        assert!(ret.is_err());
    }
}
```

# to_value in sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/0.5.8/sonic_rs/fn.to_value.html

## Expand description

Convert a `T` into `sonic_rs::Value` which can represent any valid JSON data.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use serde::Serialize;
use sonic_rs::{json, to_value, Value};
#[derive(Serialize, Debug)]
struct User {
    string: String,
    number: i32,
    array: Vec<String>,
}
 let user = User{
     string: "hello".into(),
     number: 123,
     array: vec!["a".into(), "b".into(), "c".into()],
 };
 let got: Value = sonic_rs::to_value(&user).unwrap();
 let expect = json!({
     "string": "hello",
     "number": 123,
     "array": ["a", "b", "c"],
 });
 assert_eq!(got, expect);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

This conversion can fail if `T`’s implementation of `Serialize` decides to
fail, or if `T` contains a map with non-string keys.

```
use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use sonic_rs::to_value;
// The keys in this map are vectors, not strings.
let mut map = BTreeMap::new();
map.insert(vec![32, 64], "x86");
let err = to_value(&map).unwrap_err().to_string();
assert!(err.contains("Expected the key to be string/bool/number when serializing map"));
```

# sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/latest/aarch64-apple-darwin/sonic_rs/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#sonic-rs)sonic-rs

English | [中文](https://docs.rs/README_ZH.md)

A fast Rust JSON library based on SIMD. It has some references to other open-source libraries like [sonic_cpp](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic-cpp), [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), [sonic](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic), [simdjson](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson), [rust-std](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/tree/master/library/core/src/num) and more.

**For Golang users to use  sonic_rs, please see  for_Golang_user.md**

**For users to migrate from  serde_json to sonic_rs, can see **

[serdejson_compatibility](https://github.com/cloudwego/sonic-rs/blob/main/docs/serdejson_compatibility.md)

[§](https://docs.rs#requirementsnotes)Requirements/Notes

-
Faster in x86_64 or aarch64, other architecture is fallback and maybe very slower.
-
~~Requires Rust nightly version~~Support Stable Rust now.
-
Please add the compile options `-C target-cpu=native`
-
Should enable `sanitize`feature to avoid false-positive if you are using LLVM-sanitizer in your program. Don’t enable this feature in production, since it will cause 30% performance loss in serialize.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-to-use-sonic-rs)Quick to use sonic-rs

To ensure that SIMD instruction is used in sonic-rs, you need to add rustflags `-C target-cpu=native` and compile on the host machine. For example, Rust flags can be configured in Cargo [config](https://docs.rs/.cargo/config.toml).

Add sonic-rs in `Cargo.toml`

```
[dependencies]
sonic-rs = "0.3"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

-
Serde into Rust struct as `serde_json`and`serde`.
-
Parse/Serialize JSON for untyped `sonic_rs::Value`, which can be mutable.
-
Get specific fields from a JSON with the blazing performance.
-
Use JSON as a lazy array or object iterator with the blazing performance.
-
Support `LazyValue`,`Number`and`RawNumber`(just like Golang’s`JsonNumber`) in default.
-
The floating parsing precision is as Rust std in default.

[§](https://docs.rs#benchmark)Benchmark

The main optimization in sonic-rs is the use of SIMD. However, we do not use the two-stage SIMD algorithms from `simd-json`. We primarily use SIMD in the following scenarios:

- parsing/serialize long JSON strings
- parsing the fraction of float number
- Getting a specific elem or field from JSON
- Skipping white spaces when parsing JSON

More details about optimization can be found in [performance.md](https://docs.rs/docs/performance.md).

Benchmarks environment:

```
Architecture:        x86_64
Model name:          Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8260 CPU @ 2.40GHz
```
AArch64 benchmark data can be found in [benchmark_aarch64.md](https://docs.rs/docs/benchmark_aarch64.md).

Benchmarks:

-
Deserialize Struct: Deserialize the JSON into Rust struct. The defined struct and testdata is from [json-benchmark](https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark)
-
Deseirlize Untyped: Deseialize the JSON into an untyped document

The serialize benchmarks work oppositely.

All deserialized benchmarks enabled UTF-8 validation and enabled `float_roundtrip` in `serde-json` to get sufficient precision as Rust std.

[§](https://docs.rs#deserialize-struct)Deserialize Struct

The benchmark will parse JSON into a Rust struct, and there are no unknown fields in JSON text. All fields are parsed into struct fields in the JSON.

Sonic-rs is faster than simd-json because simd-json (Rust) first parses the JSON into a `tape`, then parses the `tape` into a Rust struct. Sonic-rs directly parses the JSON into a Rust struct, and there are no temporary data structures. The [flamegraph](https://docs.rs/assets/pngs/) is profiled in the citm_catalog case.

[§](https://docs.rs#deserialize-untyped)Deserialize Untyped

The benchmark will parse JSON into a document. Sonic-rs seems faster for several reasons:

- There are also no temporary data structures in sonic-rs, as detailed above.
- Sonic-rs uses a memory arena for the whole document, resulting in fewer memory allocations, better cache-friendliness, and mutability.
- The JSON object in `sonic_rs::Value`is an array. Sonic-rs does not build a hashmap.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-into-rust-type)Serde into Rust Type

Directly use the `Deserialize` or `Serialize` trait.

```
use sonic_rs::{Deserialize, Serialize};
// sonic-rs re-exported them from serde
// or use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Person {
    name: String,
    age: u8,
    phones: Vec<String>,
}
fn main() {
    let data = r#"{
  "name": "Xiaoming",
  "age": 18,
  "phones": [
    "+123456"
  ]
}"#;
    let p: Person = sonic_rs::from_str(data).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.age, 18);
    assert_eq!(p.name, "Xiaoming");
    let out = sonic_rs::to_string_pretty(&p).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out, data);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#get-a-field-from-json)Get a field from JSON

Get a specific field from a JSON with the `pointer` path. The return is a `LazyValue`, which is a wrapper of a raw valid JSON slice.

We provide the `get` and `get_unchecked` apis. `get_unchecked` apis should be used in valid JSON, otherwise it may return unexpected result.

```
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
use sonic_rs::{get, get_unchecked, pointer};
fn main() {
    let path = pointer!["a", "b", "c", 1];
    let json = r#"
        {"u": 123, "a": {"b" : {"c": [null, "found"]}}}
    "#;
    let target = unsafe { get_unchecked(json, &path).unwrap() };
    assert_eq!(target.as_raw_str(), r#""found""#);
    assert_eq!(target.as_str().unwrap(), "found");
    let target = get(json, &path);
    assert_eq!(target.as_str().unwrap(), "found");
    assert_eq!(target.unwrap().as_raw_str(), r#""found""#);
    let path = pointer!["a", "b", "c", "d"];
    let json = r#"
        {"u": 123, "a": {"b" : {"c": [null, "found"]}}}
    "#;
    // not found from json
    let target = get(json, &path);
    assert!(target.is_err());
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parse-and-serialize-into-untyped-value)Parse and Serialize into untyped Value

Parse a JSON into a `sonic_rs::Value`.

```
use sonic_rs::{from_str, json};
use sonic_rs::JsonValueMutTrait;
use sonic_rs::{pointer, JsonValueTrait, Value};
fn main() {
    let json = r#"{
        "name": "Xiaoming",
        "obj": {},
        "arr": [],
        "age": 18,
        "address": {
            "city": "Beijing"
        },
        "phones": [
            "+123456"
        ]
    }"#;
    let mut root: Value = from_str(json).unwrap();
    // get key from value
    let age = root.get("age").as_i64();
    assert_eq!(age.unwrap_or_default(), 18);
    // get by index
    let first = root["phones"][0].as_str().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(first, "+123456");
    // get by pointer
    let phones = root.pointer(&pointer!["phones", 0]);
    assert_eq!(phones.as_str().unwrap(), "+123456");
    // convert to mutable object
    let obj = root.as_object_mut().unwrap();
    obj.insert(&"inserted", true);
    assert!(obj.contains_key(&"inserted"));
    let mut object = json!({ "A": 65, "B": 66, "C": 67 });
    *object.get_mut("A").unwrap() = json!({
        "code": 123,
        "success": false,
        "payload": {}
    });
    let mut val = json!(["A", "B", "C"]);
    *val.get_mut(2).unwrap() = json!("D");
    // serialize
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&val).unwrap(), r#"["A","B","D"]"#);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json-iterator)JSON Iterator

Parse an object or array JSON into a lazy iterator.

```
use bytes::Bytes;
use faststr::FastStr;
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
use sonic_rs::{to_array_iter, to_object_iter_unchecked};
fn main() {
    let json = Bytes::from(r#"[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]"#);
    let iter = to_array_iter(&json);
    for (i, v) in iter.enumerate() {
        assert_eq!(i + 1, v.as_u64().unwrap() as usize);
    }
    let json = Bytes::from(r#"[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6"#);
    let iter = to_array_iter(&json);
    for elem in iter {
        // do something for each elem
        // deal with errors when invalid json
        if elem.is_err() {
            assert_eq!(
                elem.err().unwrap().to_string(),
                "Expected this character to be either a ',' or a ']' while parsing at line 1 column 17"
            );
        }
    }
    let json = FastStr::from(r#"{"a": null, "b":[1, 2, 3]}"#);
    let iter = unsafe { to_object_iter_unchecked(&json) };
    for ret in iter {
        // deal with errors
        if ret.is_err() {
            println!("{}", ret.unwrap_err());
            return;
        }
        let (k, v) = ret.unwrap();
        if k == "a" {
            assert!(v.is_null());
        } else if k == "b" {
            let iter = to_array_iter(v.as_raw_str());
            for (i, v) in iter.enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(i + 1, v.as_u64().unwrap() as usize);
            }
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json-lazyvalue--number--rawnumber)JSON LazyValue & Number & RawNumber

If we need to parse a JSON value as a raw string, we can use `LazyValue`.

If we need to parse a JSON number into an untyped type, we can use `Number`.

If we need to parse a JSON number * without loss of precision*, we can use

`RawNumber`. It likes `encoding/json.Number` in Golang, and can also be parsed from a JSON string.Detailed examples can be found in [raw_value.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/raw_value.rs) and [json_number.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/json_number.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#error-handle)Error handle

Sonic’s errors are followed as `serde-json` and have a display around the error position, examples in [handle_error.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/handle_error.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#faqs)FAQs

[§](https://docs.rs#about-utf-8)About UTF-8

By default, sonic-rs enable the UTF-8 validation, except for `xx_unchecked` APIs.

[§](https://docs.rs#about-floating-point-precision)About floating point precision

By default, sonic-rs uses floating point precision consistent with the Rust standard library, and there is no need to add an extra `float_roundtrip` feature like `serde-json` to ensure floating point precision.

If you want to achieve lossless precision when parsing floating-point numbers, such as Golang `encoding/json.Number` and `serde-json arbitrary_precision`, you can use `sonic_rs::RawNumber`.

[§](https://docs.rs#acknowledgement)Acknowledgement

Thanks the following open-source libraries. sonic-rs has some references to other open-source libraries like [sonic_cpp](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic-cpp), [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), [sonic](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic), [simdjson](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson), [yyjson](https://github.com/ibireme/yyjson), [rust-std](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/tree/master/library/core/src/num) and so on.

We rewrote many SIMD algorithms from sonic-cpp/sonic/simdjson/yyjson for performance. We reused the de/ser codes and modified necessary parts from serde_json to make high compatibility with `serde`. We reused part codes about floating parsing from rust-std to make it more accurate.

Referenced papers:

- [Parsing Gigabytes of JSON per Second](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.08318)
- [JSONSki: streaming semi-structured data with bit-parallel fast-forwarding](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3503222.3507719)

- get_many returns multiple fields from the `PointerTree`.
- [get_](https://docs.rs/fn.get_unchecked.html)- unchecked - ⚠
- Gets a field from a `path`. And return it as a`Result<LazyValue>`
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_array_iter.html)- array_ - iter
- Traverse the JSON array text through a lazy iterator. The JSON parsing will doing when iterating.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_array_iter_unchecked.html)- array_ - iter_ - unchecked - ⚠
- Traverse the JSON text through a lazy object iterator. The JSON parsing will doing when iterating.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_lazyvalue.html)- lazyvalue
- Serialize the given data structure as a OwnedLazyValue of JSON.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_object_iter.html)- object_ - iter
- Traverse the JSON object text through a lazy iterator. The JSON parsing will doing when iterating.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_object_iter_unchecked.html)- object_ - iter_ - unchecked - ⚠
- Traverse the JSON text through a lazy object iterator. The JSON parsing will doing when iterating.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_string.html)- string
- Serialize the given data structure as a String of JSON.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_string_pretty.html)- string_ - pretty
- Serialize the given data structure as a pretty-printed String of JSON.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_value.html)- value
- Convert a `T`into`sonic_rs::Value`which can represent any valid JSON data.
- [to_vec](https://docs.rs/fn.to_vec.html)
- Serialize the given data structure as a JSON byte vector.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_vec_pretty.html)- vec_ - pretty
- Serialize the given data structure as a pretty-printed JSON byte vector.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_writer.html)- writer
- Serialize the given data structure as JSON into the I/O stream.
- [to_](https://docs.rs/fn.to_writer_pretty.html)- writer_ - pretty
- Serialize the given data structure as pretty-printed JSON into the I/O stream.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Json](https://docs.rs/type.JsonPointer.html)- Pointer
- Represents a json pointer path. It can be created by [`pointer!`] macro.
- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- Alias for a `Result`with the error type`sonic_rs::Error`.

# sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/latest/aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu/sonic_rs/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#sonic-rs)sonic-rs

English | [中文](https://docs.rs/README_ZH.md)

A fast Rust JSON library based on SIMD. It has some references to other open-source libraries like [sonic_cpp](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic-cpp), [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), [sonic](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic), [simdjson](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson), [rust-std](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/tree/master/library/core/src/num) and more.

**For Golang users to use  sonic_rs, please see  for_Golang_user.md**

**For users to migrate from  serde_json to sonic_rs, can see **

[serdejson_compatibility](https://github.com/cloudwego/sonic-rs/blob/main/docs/serdejson_compatibility.md)

[§](https://docs.rs#requirementsnotes)Requirements/Notes

-
Faster in x86_64 or aarch64, other architecture is fallback and maybe very slower.
-
~~Requires Rust nightly version~~Support Stable Rust now.
-
Please add the compile options `-C target-cpu=native`
-
Should enable `sanitize`feature to avoid false-positive if you are using LLVM-sanitizer in your program. Don’t enable this feature in production, since it will cause 30% performance loss in serialize.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-to-use-sonic-rs)Quick to use sonic-rs

To ensure that SIMD instruction is used in sonic-rs, you need to add rustflags `-C target-cpu=native` and compile on the host machine. For example, Rust flags can be configured in Cargo [config](https://docs.rs/.cargo/config.toml).

Add sonic-rs in `Cargo.toml`

```
[dependencies]
sonic-rs = "0.3"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

-
Serde into Rust struct as `serde_json`and`serde`.
-
Parse/Serialize JSON for untyped `sonic_rs::Value`, which can be mutable.
-
Get specific fields from a JSON with the blazing performance.
-
Use JSON as a lazy array or object iterator with the blazing performance.
-
Support `LazyValue`,`Number`and`RawNumber`(just like Golang’s`JsonNumber`) in default.
-
The floating parsing precision is as Rust std in default.

[§](https://docs.rs#benchmark)Benchmark

The main optimization in sonic-rs is the use of SIMD. However, we do not use the two-stage SIMD algorithms from `simd-json`. We primarily use SIMD in the following scenarios:

- parsing/serialize long JSON strings
- parsing the fraction of float number
- Getting a specific elem or field from JSON
- Skipping white spaces when parsing JSON

More details about optimization can be found in [performance.md](https://docs.rs/docs/performance.md).

Benchmarks environment:

```
Architecture:        x86_64
Model name:          Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8260 CPU @ 2.40GHz
```
AArch64 benchmark data can be found in [benchmark_aarch64.md](https://docs.rs/docs/benchmark_aarch64.md).

Benchmarks:

-
Deserialize Struct: Deserialize the JSON into Rust struct. The defined struct and testdata is from [json-benchmark](https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark)
-
Deseirlize Untyped: Deseialize the JSON into an untyped document

The serialize benchmarks work oppositely.

All deserialized benchmarks enabled UTF-8 validation and enabled `float_roundtrip` in `serde-json` to get sufficient precision as Rust std.

[§](https://docs.rs#deserialize-struct)Deserialize Struct

The benchmark will parse JSON into a Rust struct, and there are no unknown fields in JSON text. All fields are parsed into struct fields in the JSON.

Sonic-rs is faster than simd-json because simd-json (Rust) first parses the JSON into a `tape`, then parses the `tape` into a Rust struct. Sonic-rs directly parses the JSON into a Rust struct, and there are no temporary data structures. The [flamegraph](https://docs.rs/assets/pngs/) is profiled in the citm_catalog case.

[§](https://docs.rs#deserialize-untyped)Deserialize Untyped

The benchmark will parse JSON into a document. Sonic-rs seems faster for several reasons:

- There are also no temporary data structures in sonic-rs, as detailed above.
- Sonic-rs uses a memory arena for the whole document, resulting in fewer memory allocations, better cache-friendliness, and mutability.
- The JSON object in `sonic_rs::Value`is an array. Sonic-rs does not build a hashmap.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-into-rust-type)Serde into Rust Type

Directly use the `Deserialize` or `Serialize` trait.

```
use sonic_rs::{Deserialize, Serialize};
// sonic-rs re-exported them from serde
// or use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Person {
    name: String,
    age: u8,
    phones: Vec<String>,
}
fn main() {
    let data = r#"{
  "name": "Xiaoming",
  "age": 18,
  "phones": [
    "+123456"
  ]
}"#;
    let p: Person = sonic_rs::from_str(data).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.age, 18);
    assert_eq!(p.name, "Xiaoming");
    let out = sonic_rs::to_string_pretty(&p).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out, data);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#get-a-field-from-json)Get a field from JSON

Get a specific field from a JSON with the `pointer` path. The return is a `LazyValue`, which is a wrapper of a raw valid JSON slice.

We provide the `get` and `get_unchecked` apis. `get_unchecked` apis should be used in valid JSON, otherwise it may return unexpected result.

```
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
use sonic_rs::{get, get_unchecked, pointer};
fn main() {
    let path = pointer!["a", "b", "c", 1];
    let json = r#"
        {"u": 123, "a": {"b" : {"c": [null, "found"]}}}
    "#;
    let target = unsafe { get_unchecked(json, &path).unwrap() };
    assert_eq!(target.as_raw_str(), r#""found""#);
    assert_eq!(target.as_str().unwrap(), "found");
    let target = get(json, &path);
    assert_eq!(target.as_str().unwrap(), "found");
    assert_eq!(target.unwrap().as_raw_str(), r#""found""#);
    let path = pointer!["a", "b", "c", "d"];
    let json = r#"
        {"u": 123, "a": {"b" : {"c": [null, "found"]}}}
    "#;
    // not found from json
    let target = get(json, &path);
    assert!(target.is_err());
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parse-and-serialize-into-untyped-value)Parse and Serialize into untyped Value

Parse a JSON into a `sonic_rs::Value`.

```
use sonic_rs::{from_str, json};
use sonic_rs::JsonValueMutTrait;
use sonic_rs::{pointer, JsonValueTrait, Value};
fn main() {
    let json = r#"{
        "name": "Xiaoming",
        "obj": {},
        "arr": [],
        "age": 18,
        "address": {
            "city": "Beijing"
        },
        "phones": [
            "+123456"
        ]
    }"#;
    let mut root: Value = from_str(json).unwrap();
    // get key from value
    let age = root.get("age").as_i64();
    assert_eq!(age.unwrap_or_default(), 18);
    // get by index
    let first = root["phones"][0].as_str().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(first, "+123456");
    // get by pointer
    let phones = root.pointer(&pointer!["phones", 0]);
    assert_eq!(phones.as_str().unwrap(), "+123456");
    // convert to mutable object
    let obj = root.as_object_mut().unwrap();
    obj.insert(&"inserted", true);
    assert!(obj.contains_key(&"inserted"));
    let mut object = json!({ "A": 65, "B": 66, "C": 67 });
    *object.get_mut("A").unwrap() = json!({
        "code": 123,
        "success": false,
        "payload": {}
    });
    let mut val = json!(["A", "B", "C"]);
    *val.get_mut(2).unwrap() = json!("D");
    // serialize
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&val).unwrap(), r#"["A","B","D"]"#);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json-iterator)JSON Iterator

Parse an object or array JSON into a lazy iterator.

```
use bytes::Bytes;
use faststr::FastStr;
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
use sonic_rs::{to_array_iter, to_object_iter_unchecked};
fn main() {
    let json = Bytes::from(r#"[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]"#);
    let iter = to_array_iter(&json);
    for (i, v) in iter.enumerate() {
        assert_eq!(i + 1, v.as_u64().unwrap() as usize);
    }
    let json = Bytes::from(r#"[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6"#);
    let iter = to_array_iter(&json);
    for elem in iter {
        // do something for each elem
        // deal with errors when invalid json
        if elem.is_err() {
            assert_eq!(
                elem.err().unwrap().to_string(),
                "Expected this character to be either a ',' or a ']' while parsing at line 1 column 17"
            );
        }
    }
    let json = FastStr::from(r#"{"a": null, "b":[1, 2, 3]}"#);
    let iter = unsafe { to_object_iter_unchecked(&json) };
    for ret in iter {
        // deal with errors
        if ret.is_err() {
            println!("{}", ret.unwrap_err());
            return;
        }
        let (k, v) = ret.unwrap();
        if k == "a" {
            assert!(v.is_null());
        } else if k == "b" {
            let iter = to_array_iter(v.as_raw_str());
            for (i, v) in iter.enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(i + 1, v.as_u64().unwrap() as usize);
            }
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json-lazyvalue--number--rawnumber)JSON LazyValue & Number & RawNumber

If we need to parse a JSON value as a raw string, we can use `LazyValue`.

If we need to parse a JSON number into an untyped type, we can use `Number`.

If we need to parse a JSON number * without loss of precision*, we can use

`RawNumber`. It likes `encoding/json.Number` in Golang, and can also be parsed from a JSON string.Detailed examples can be found in [raw_value.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/raw_value.rs) and [json_number.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/json_number.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#error-handle)Error handle

Sonic’s errors are followed as `serde-json` and have a display around the error position, examples in [handle_error.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/handle_error.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#faqs)FAQs

[§](https://docs.rs#about-utf-8)About UTF-8

By default, sonic-rs enable the UTF-8 validation, except for `xx_unchecked` APIs.

[§](https://docs.rs#about-floating-point-precision)About floating point precision

By default, sonic-rs uses floating point precision consistent with the Rust standard library, and there is no need to add an extra `float_roundtrip` feature like `serde-json` to ensure floating point precision.

If you want to achieve lossless precision when parsing floating-point numbers, such as Golang `encoding/json.Number` and `serde-json arbitrary_precision`, you can use `sonic_rs::RawNumber`.

[§](https://docs.rs#acknowledgement)Acknowledgement

Thanks the following open-source libraries. sonic-rs has some references to other open-source libraries like [sonic_cpp](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic-cpp), [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), [sonic](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic), [simdjson](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson), [yyjson](https://github.com/ibireme/yyjson), [rust-std](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/tree/master/library/core/src/num) and so on.

We rewrote many SIMD algorithms from sonic-cpp/sonic/simdjson/yyjson for performance. We reused the de/ser codes and modified necessary parts from serde_json to make high compatibility with `serde`. We reused part codes about floating parsing from rust-std to make it more accurate.

Referenced papers:

- [Parsing Gigabytes of JSON per Second](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.08318)
- [JSONSki: streaming semi-structured data with bit-parallel fast-forwarding](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3503222.3507719)

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md) for information on contributing to sonic-rs.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.Array.html)
- Array represents a JSON array. Its APIs are likes `Array<Value>`.
- [Array](https://docs.rs/struct.ArrayJsonIter.html)- Json - Iter
- A lazied iterator for JSON array text. It will parse the JSON when iterating.
- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/struct.Deserializer.html)
- A structure that deserializes JSON into Rust values.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- This type represents all possible errors that can occur when serializing or deserializing JSON data.
- [FastStr](https://docs.rs/struct.FastStr.html)
- `FastStr`is a string type that try to avoid the cost of clone.
- [Lazy](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyArray.html)- Array
- [Lazy](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyObject.html)- Object
- [Lazy](https://docs.rs/struct.LazyValue.html)- Value
- LazyValue wrappers a unparsed raw JSON text. It is borrowed from the origin JSON text.
- [MapAccess](https://docs.rs/struct.MapAccess.html)
- [Number](https://docs.rs/struct.Number.html)
- Represents a JSON number, whether integer or floating point.
- [Object](https://docs.rs/struct.Object.html)
- Represents the JSON object. The inner implement is a key-value array. Its order is as same as origin JSON.
- [Object](https://docs.rs/struct.ObjectJsonIter.html)- Json - Iter
- A lazied iterator for JSON object text. It will parse the JSON when iterating.
- [Owned](https://docs.rs/struct.OwnedLazyValue.html)- Lazy - Value
- OwnedLazyValue wrappers a unparsed raw JSON text. It is owned and support `Get, Set`
- [Pointer](https://docs.rs/struct.PointerTree.html)- Tree
- PointerTree is designed for `get_many``get_many_unchecked`
- [RawNumber](https://docs.rs/struct.RawNumber.html)
- Represents a JSON number with arbitrary precision, the underlying representation of a string,
like as Golang `json.Number`.
- [Read](https://docs.rs/struct.Read.html)
- JSON input source that reads from a string/bytes-like JSON input.
- [SeqAccess](https://docs.rs/struct.SeqAccess.html)
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/struct.Serializer.html)
- A structure for serializing Rust values into JSON.
- [Stream](https://docs.rs/struct.StreamDeserializer.html)- Deserializer
- An iterator that deserializes a json stream into multiple `T`values.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/struct.Value.html)
- Represents any valid JSON value.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Json](https://docs.rs/enum.JsonType.html)- Type
- JsonType is an enum that represents the type of a JSON value.
- [Pointer](https://docs.rs/enum.PointerNode.html)- Node
- Represents a node in a json pointer path.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/enum.ValueRef.html)- Ref
- ValueRef is a immutable reference helper for `Value`.

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde.
- [Index](https://docs.rs/trait.Index.html)
- An indexing trait for JSON.
- [Json](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonContainerTrait.html)- Container - Trait
- A trait for all JSON object or array values. Used by `Value`.
- [Json](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonInput.html)- Input
- A trait for string/bytes-like types that can be parsed into JSON.
- [Json](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonNumberTrait.html)- Number - Trait
- Number trait for both `Number`and`RawNumber`.
- [Json](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueMutTrait.html)- Value - MutTrait
- A trait for all mutable JSON values. Used by mutable `Value`.
- [Json](https://docs.rs/trait.JsonValueTrait.html)- Value - Trait
- A trait for all JSON values. Used by `Value`and`LazyValue`.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be serialized into any data format supported by Serde.

# sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/latest/x86_64-pc-windows-msvc/sonic_rs/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#sonic-rs)sonic-rs

English | [中文](https://docs.rs/README_ZH.md)

A fast Rust JSON library based on SIMD. It has some references to other open-source libraries like [sonic_cpp](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic-cpp), [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), [sonic](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic), [simdjson](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson), [rust-std](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/tree/master/library/core/src/num) and more.

**For Golang users to use  sonic_rs, please see  for_Golang_user.md**

**For users to migrate from  serde_json to sonic_rs, can see **

[serdejson_compatibility](https://github.com/cloudwego/sonic-rs/blob/main/docs/serdejson_compatibility.md)

[§](https://docs.rs#requirementsnotes)Requirements/Notes

-
Faster in x86_64 or aarch64, other architecture is fallback and maybe very slower.
-
~~Requires Rust nightly version~~Support Stable Rust now.
-
Please add the compile options `-C target-cpu=native`
-
Should enable `sanitize`feature to avoid false-positive if you are using LLVM-sanitizer in your program. Don’t enable this feature in production, since it will cause 30% performance loss in serialize.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-to-use-sonic-rs)Quick to use sonic-rs

To ensure that SIMD instruction is used in sonic-rs, you need to add rustflags `-C target-cpu=native` and compile on the host machine. For example, Rust flags can be configured in Cargo [config](https://docs.rs/.cargo/config.toml).

Add sonic-rs in `Cargo.toml`

```
[dependencies]
sonic-rs = "0.3"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

-
Serde into Rust struct as `serde_json`and`serde`.
-
Parse/Serialize JSON for untyped `sonic_rs::Value`, which can be mutable.
-
Get specific fields from a JSON with the blazing performance.
-
Use JSON as a lazy array or object iterator with the blazing performance.
-
Support `LazyValue`,`Number`and`RawNumber`(just like Golang’s`JsonNumber`) in default.
-
The floating parsing precision is as Rust std in default.

[§](https://docs.rs#benchmark)Benchmark

The main optimization in sonic-rs is the use of SIMD. However, we do not use the two-stage SIMD algorithms from `simd-json`. We primarily use SIMD in the following scenarios:

- parsing/serialize long JSON strings
- parsing the fraction of float number
- Getting a specific elem or field from JSON
- Skipping white spaces when parsing JSON

More details about optimization can be found in [performance.md](https://docs.rs/docs/performance.md).

Benchmarks environment:

```
Architecture:        x86_64
Model name:          Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8260 CPU @ 2.40GHz
```
AArch64 benchmark data can be found in [benchmark_aarch64.md](https://docs.rs/docs/benchmark_aarch64.md).

Benchmarks:

-
Deserialize Struct: Deserialize the JSON into Rust struct. The defined struct and testdata is from [json-benchmark](https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark)
-
Deseirlize Untyped: Deseialize the JSON into an untyped document

The serialize benchmarks work oppositely.

All deserialized benchmarks enabled UTF-8 validation and enabled `float_roundtrip` in `serde-json` to get sufficient precision as Rust std.

[§](https://docs.rs#deserialize-struct)Deserialize Struct

The benchmark will parse JSON into a Rust struct, and there are no unknown fields in JSON text. All fields are parsed into struct fields in the JSON.

Sonic-rs is faster than simd-json because simd-json (Rust) first parses the JSON into a `tape`, then parses the `tape` into a Rust struct. Sonic-rs directly parses the JSON into a Rust struct, and there are no temporary data structures. The [flamegraph](https://docs.rs/assets/pngs/) is profiled in the citm_catalog case.

[§](https://docs.rs#deserialize-untyped)Deserialize Untyped

The benchmark will parse JSON into a document. Sonic-rs seems faster for several reasons:

- There are also no temporary data structures in sonic-rs, as detailed above.
- Sonic-rs uses a memory arena for the whole document, resulting in fewer memory allocations, better cache-friendliness, and mutability.
- The JSON object in `sonic_rs::Value`is an array. Sonic-rs does not build a hashmap.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-into-rust-type)Serde into Rust Type

Directly use the `Deserialize` or `Serialize` trait.

```
use sonic_rs::{Deserialize, Serialize};
// sonic-rs re-exported them from serde
// or use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Person {
    name: String,
    age: u8,
    phones: Vec<String>,
}
fn main() {
    let data = r#"{
  "name": "Xiaoming",
  "age": 18,
  "phones": [
    "+123456"
  ]
}"#;
    let p: Person = sonic_rs::from_str(data).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.age, 18);
    assert_eq!(p.name, "Xiaoming");
    let out = sonic_rs::to_string_pretty(&p).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out, data);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#get-a-field-from-json)Get a field from JSON

Get a specific field from a JSON with the `pointer` path. The return is a `LazyValue`, which is a wrapper of a raw valid JSON slice.

We provide the `get` and `get_unchecked` apis. `get_unchecked` apis should be used in valid JSON, otherwise it may return unexpected result.

```
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
use sonic_rs::{get, get_unchecked, pointer};
fn main() {
    let path = pointer!["a", "b", "c", 1];
    let json = r#"
        {"u": 123, "a": {"b" : {"c": [null, "found"]}}}
    "#;
    let target = unsafe { get_unchecked(json, &path).unwrap() };
    assert_eq!(target.as_raw_str(), r#""found""#);
    assert_eq!(target.as_str().unwrap(), "found");
    let target = get(json, &path);
    assert_eq!(target.as_str().unwrap(), "found");
    assert_eq!(target.unwrap().as_raw_str(), r#""found""#);
    let path = pointer!["a", "b", "c", "d"];
    let json = r#"
        {"u": 123, "a": {"b" : {"c": [null, "found"]}}}
    "#;
    // not found from json
    let target = get(json, &path);
    assert!(target.is_err());
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parse-and-serialize-into-untyped-value)Parse and Serialize into untyped Value

Parse a JSON into a `sonic_rs::Value`.

```
use sonic_rs::{from_str, json};
use sonic_rs::JsonValueMutTrait;
use sonic_rs::{pointer, JsonValueTrait, Value};
fn main() {
    let json = r#"{
        "name": "Xiaoming",
        "obj": {},
        "arr": [],
        "age": 18,
        "address": {
            "city": "Beijing"
        },
        "phones": [
            "+123456"
        ]
    }"#;
    let mut root: Value = from_str(json).unwrap();
    // get key from value
    let age = root.get("age").as_i64();
    assert_eq!(age.unwrap_or_default(), 18);
    // get by index
    let first = root["phones"][0].as_str().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(first, "+123456");
    // get by pointer
    let phones = root.pointer(&pointer!["phones", 0]);
    assert_eq!(phones.as_str().unwrap(), "+123456");
    // convert to mutable object
    let obj = root.as_object_mut().unwrap();
    obj.insert(&"inserted", true);
    assert!(obj.contains_key(&"inserted"));
    let mut object = json!({ "A": 65, "B": 66, "C": 67 });
    *object.get_mut("A").unwrap() = json!({
        "code": 123,
        "success": false,
        "payload": {}
    });
    let mut val = json!(["A", "B", "C"]);
    *val.get_mut(2).unwrap() = json!("D");
    // serialize
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&val).unwrap(), r#"["A","B","D"]"#);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json-iterator)JSON Iterator

Parse an object or array JSON into a lazy iterator.

```
use bytes::Bytes;
use faststr::FastStr;
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
use sonic_rs::{to_array_iter, to_object_iter_unchecked};
fn main() {
    let json = Bytes::from(r#"[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]"#);
    let iter = to_array_iter(&json);
    for (i, v) in iter.enumerate() {
        assert_eq!(i + 1, v.as_u64().unwrap() as usize);
    }
    let json = Bytes::from(r#"[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6"#);
    let iter = to_array_iter(&json);
    for elem in iter {
        // do something for each elem
        // deal with errors when invalid json
        if elem.is_err() {
            assert_eq!(
                elem.err().unwrap().to_string(),
                "Expected this character to be either a ',' or a ']' while parsing at line 1 column 17"
            );
        }
    }
    let json = FastStr::from(r#"{"a": null, "b":[1, 2, 3]}"#);
    let iter = unsafe { to_object_iter_unchecked(&json) };
    for ret in iter {
        // deal with errors
        if ret.is_err() {
            println!("{}", ret.unwrap_err());
            return;
        }
        let (k, v) = ret.unwrap();
        if k == "a" {
            assert!(v.is_null());
        } else if k == "b" {
            let iter = to_array_iter(v.as_raw_str());
            for (i, v) in iter.enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(i + 1, v.as_u64().unwrap() as usize);
            }
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json-lazyvalue--number--rawnumber)JSON LazyValue & Number & RawNumber

If we need to parse a JSON value as a raw string, we can use `LazyValue`.

If we need to parse a JSON number into an untyped type, we can use `Number`.

If we need to parse a JSON number * without loss of precision*, we can use

`RawNumber`. It likes `encoding/json.Number` in Golang, and can also be parsed from a JSON string.Detailed examples can be found in [raw_value.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/raw_value.rs) and [json_number.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/json_number.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#error-handle)Error handle

Sonic’s errors are followed as `serde-json` and have a display around the error position, examples in [handle_error.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/handle_error.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#faqs)FAQs

[§](https://docs.rs#about-utf-8)About UTF-8

By default, sonic-rs enable the UTF-8 validation, except for `xx_unchecked` APIs.

[§](https://docs.rs#about-floating-point-precision)About floating point precision

By default, sonic-rs uses floating point precision consistent with the Rust standard library, and there is no need to add an extra `float_roundtrip` feature like `serde-json` to ensure floating point precision.

If you want to achieve lossless precision when parsing floating-point numbers, such as Golang `encoding/json.Number` and `serde-json arbitrary_precision`, you can use `sonic_rs::RawNumber`.

[§](https://docs.rs#acknowledgement)Acknowledgement

Thanks the following open-source libraries. sonic-rs has some references to other open-source libraries like [sonic_cpp](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic-cpp), [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), [sonic](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic), [simdjson](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson), [yyjson](https://github.com/ibireme/yyjson), [rust-std](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/tree/master/library/core/src/num) and so on.

We rewrote many SIMD algorithms from sonic-cpp/sonic/simdjson/yyjson for performance. We reused the de/ser codes and modified necessary parts from serde_json to make high compatibility with `serde`. We reused part codes about floating parsing from rust-std to make it more accurate.

Referenced papers:

- [Parsing Gigabytes of JSON per Second](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.08318)
- [JSONSki: streaming semi-structured data with bit-parallel fast-forwarding](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3503222.3507719)

[§](https://docs.rs#contributing)Contributing

Please read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://docs.rs/CONTRIBUTING.md) for information on contributing to sonic-rs.

# sonic_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sonic-rs/latest/sonic_rs/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#sonic-rs)sonic-rs

English | [中文](https://docs.rs/README_ZH.md)

A fast Rust JSON library based on SIMD. It has some references to other open-source libraries like [sonic_cpp](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic-cpp), [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), [sonic](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic), [simdjson](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson), [rust-std](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/tree/master/library/core/src/num) and more.

**For Golang users to use  sonic_rs, please see  for_Golang_user.md**

**For users to migrate from  serde_json to sonic_rs, can see **

[serdejson_compatibility](https://github.com/cloudwego/sonic-rs/blob/main/docs/serdejson_compatibility.md)

[§](https://docs.rs#requirementsnotes)Requirements/Notes

-
Faster in x86_64 or aarch64, other architecture is fallback and maybe very slower.
-
~~Requires Rust nightly version~~Support Stable Rust now.
-
Please add the compile options `-C target-cpu=native`
-
Should enable `sanitize`feature to avoid false-positive if you are using LLVM-sanitizer in your program. Don’t enable this feature in production, since it will cause 30% performance loss in serialize.

[§](https://docs.rs#quick-to-use-sonic-rs)Quick to use sonic-rs

To ensure that SIMD instruction is used in sonic-rs, you need to add rustflags `-C target-cpu=native` and compile on the host machine. For example, Rust flags can be configured in Cargo [config](https://docs.rs/.cargo/config.toml).

Add sonic-rs in `Cargo.toml`

```
[dependencies]
sonic-rs = "0.3"
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

-
Serde into Rust struct as `serde_json`and`serde`.
-
Parse/Serialize JSON for untyped `sonic_rs::Value`, which can be mutable.
-
Get specific fields from a JSON with the blazing performance.
-
Use JSON as a lazy array or object iterator with the blazing performance.
-
Support `LazyValue`,`Number`and`RawNumber`(just like Golang’s`JsonNumber`) in default.
-
The floating parsing precision is as Rust std in default.

[§](https://docs.rs#benchmark)Benchmark

The main optimization in sonic-rs is the use of SIMD. However, we do not use the two-stage SIMD algorithms from `simd-json`. We primarily use SIMD in the following scenarios:

- parsing/serialize long JSON strings
- parsing the fraction of float number
- Getting a specific elem or field from JSON
- Skipping white spaces when parsing JSON

More details about optimization can be found in [performance.md](https://docs.rs/docs/performance.md).

Benchmarks environment:

```
Architecture:        x86_64
Model name:          Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8260 CPU @ 2.40GHz
```
AArch64 benchmark data can be found in [benchmark_aarch64.md](https://docs.rs/docs/benchmark_aarch64.md).

Benchmarks:

-
Deserialize Struct: Deserialize the JSON into Rust struct. The defined struct and testdata is from [json-benchmark](https://github.com/serde-rs/json-benchmark)
-
Deseirlize Untyped: Deseialize the JSON into an untyped document

The serialize benchmarks work oppositely.

All deserialized benchmarks enabled UTF-8 validation and enabled `float_roundtrip` in `serde-json` to get sufficient precision as Rust std.

[§](https://docs.rs#deserialize-struct)Deserialize Struct

The benchmark will parse JSON into a Rust struct, and there are no unknown fields in JSON text. All fields are parsed into struct fields in the JSON.

Sonic-rs is faster than simd-json because simd-json (Rust) first parses the JSON into a `tape`, then parses the `tape` into a Rust struct. Sonic-rs directly parses the JSON into a Rust struct, and there are no temporary data structures. The [flamegraph](https://docs.rs/assets/pngs/) is profiled in the citm_catalog case.

`cargo bench --bench deserialize_struct -- --quiet`

[§](https://docs.rs#deserialize-untyped)Deserialize Untyped

The benchmark will parse JSON into a document. Sonic-rs seems faster for several reasons:

- There are also no temporary data structures in sonic-rs, as detailed above.
- Sonic-rs uses a memory arena for the whole document, resulting in fewer memory allocations, better cache-friendliness, and mutability.
- The JSON object in `sonic_rs::Value`is an array. Sonic-rs does not build a hashmap.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-into-rust-type)Serde into Rust Type

Directly use the `Deserialize` or `Serialize` trait.

```
use sonic_rs::{Deserialize, Serialize};
// sonic-rs re-exported them from serde
// or use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct Person {
    name: String,
    age: u8,
    phones: Vec<String>,
}
fn main() {
    let data = r#"{
  "name": "Xiaoming",
  "age": 18,
  "phones": [
    "+123456"
  ]
}"#;
    let p: Person = sonic_rs::from_str(data).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(p.age, 18);
    assert_eq!(p.name, "Xiaoming");
    let out = sonic_rs::to_string_pretty(&p).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(out, data);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#get-a-field-from-json)Get a field from JSON

Get a specific field from a JSON with the `pointer` path. The return is a `LazyValue`, which is a wrapper of a raw valid JSON slice.

We provide the `get` and `get_unchecked` apis. `get_unchecked` apis should be used in valid JSON, otherwise it may return unexpected result.

```
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
use sonic_rs::{get, get_unchecked, pointer};
fn main() {
    let path = pointer!["a", "b", "c", 1];
    let json = r#"
        {"u": 123, "a": {"b" : {"c": [null, "found"]}}}
    "#;
    let target = unsafe { get_unchecked(json, &path).unwrap() };
    assert_eq!(target.as_raw_str(), r#""found""#);
    assert_eq!(target.as_str().unwrap(), "found");
    let target = get(json, &path);
    assert_eq!(target.as_str().unwrap(), "found");
    assert_eq!(target.unwrap().as_raw_str(), r#""found""#);
    let path = pointer!["a", "b", "c", "d"];
    let json = r#"
        {"u": 123, "a": {"b" : {"c": [null, "found"]}}}
    "#;
    // not found from json
    let target = get(json, &path);
    assert!(target.is_err());
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#parse-and-serialize-into-untyped-value)Parse and Serialize into untyped Value

Parse a JSON into a `sonic_rs::Value`.

```
use sonic_rs::{from_str, json};
use sonic_rs::JsonValueMutTrait;
use sonic_rs::{pointer, JsonValueTrait, Value};
fn main() {
    let json = r#"{
        "name": "Xiaoming",
        "obj": {},
        "arr": [],
        "age": 18,
        "address": {
            "city": "Beijing"
        },
        "phones": [
            "+123456"
        ]
    }"#;
    let mut root: Value = from_str(json).unwrap();
    // get key from value
    let age = root.get("age").as_i64();
    assert_eq!(age.unwrap_or_default(), 18);
    // get by index
    let first = root["phones"][0].as_str().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(first, "+123456");
    // get by pointer
    let phones = root.pointer(&pointer!["phones", 0]);
    assert_eq!(phones.as_str().unwrap(), "+123456");
    // convert to mutable object
    let obj = root.as_object_mut().unwrap();
    obj.insert(&"inserted", true);
    assert!(obj.contains_key(&"inserted"));
    let mut object = json!({ "A": 65, "B": 66, "C": 67 });
    *object.get_mut("A").unwrap() = json!({
        "code": 123,
        "success": false,
        "payload": {}
    });
    let mut val = json!(["A", "B", "C"]);
    *val.get_mut(2).unwrap() = json!("D");
    // serialize
    assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&val).unwrap(), r#"["A","B","D"]"#);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json-iterator)JSON Iterator

Parse an object or array JSON into a lazy iterator.

```
use bytes::Bytes;
use faststr::FastStr;
use sonic_rs::JsonValueTrait;
use sonic_rs::{to_array_iter, to_object_iter_unchecked};
fn main() {
    let json = Bytes::from(r#"[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]"#);
    let iter = to_array_iter(&json);
    for (i, v) in iter.enumerate() {
        assert_eq!(i + 1, v.as_u64().unwrap() as usize);
    }
    let json = Bytes::from(r#"[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6"#);
    let iter = to_array_iter(&json);
    for elem in iter {
        // do something for each elem
        // deal with errors when invalid json
        if elem.is_err() {
            assert_eq!(
                elem.err().unwrap().to_string(),
                "Expected this character to be either a ',' or a ']' while parsing at line 1 column 17"
            );
        }
    }
    let json = FastStr::from(r#"{"a": null, "b":[1, 2, 3]}"#);
    let iter = unsafe { to_object_iter_unchecked(&json) };
    for ret in iter {
        // deal with errors
        if ret.is_err() {
            println!("{}", ret.unwrap_err());
            return;
        }
        let (k, v) = ret.unwrap();
        if k == "a" {
            assert!(v.is_null());
        } else if k == "b" {
            let iter = to_array_iter(v.as_raw_str());
            for (i, v) in iter.enumerate() {
                assert_eq!(i + 1, v.as_u64().unwrap() as usize);
            }
        }
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#json-lazyvalue--number--rawnumber)JSON LazyValue & Number & RawNumber

If we need to parse a JSON value as a raw string, we can use `LazyValue`.

If we need to parse a JSON number into an untyped type, we can use `Number`.

If we need to parse a JSON number * without loss of precision*, we can use

`RawNumber`. It likes `encoding/json.Number` in Golang, and can also be parsed from a JSON string.Detailed examples can be found in [raw_value.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/raw_value.rs) and [json_number.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/json_number.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#error-handle)Error handle

Sonic’s errors are followed as `serde-json` and have a display around the error position, examples in [handle_error.rs](https://docs.rs/examples/handle_error.rs).

[§](https://docs.rs#faqs)FAQs

[§](https://docs.rs#about-utf-8)About UTF-8

By default, sonic-rs enable the UTF-8 validation, except for `xx_unchecked` APIs.

[§](https://docs.rs#about-floating-point-precision)About floating point precision

By default, sonic-rs uses floating point precision consistent with the Rust standard library, and there is no need to add an extra `float_roundtrip` feature like `serde-json` to ensure floating point precision.

If you want to achieve lossless precision when parsing floating-point numbers, such as Golang `encoding/json.Number` and `serde-json arbitrary_precision`, you can use `sonic_rs::RawNumber`.

[§](https://docs.rs#acknowledgement)Acknowledgement

Thanks the following open-source libraries. sonic-rs has some references to other open-source libraries like [sonic_cpp](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic-cpp), [serde_json](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), [sonic](https://github.com/bytedance/sonic), [simdjson](https://github.com/simdjson/simdjson), [yyjson](https://github.com/ibireme/yyjson), [rust-std](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/tree/master/library/core/src/num) and so on.

We rewrote many SIMD algorithms from sonic-cpp/sonic/simdjson/yyjson for performance. We reused the de/ser codes and modified necessary parts from serde_json to make high compatibility with `serde`. We reused part codes about floating parsing from rust-std to make it more accurate.

Referenced papers:

- [Parsing Gigabytes of JSON per Second](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.08318)
- [JSONSki: streaming semi-structured data with bit-parallel fast-forwarding](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3503222.3507719)
